messages:
emily (People Ops): Quick question from Theo: he's mid-year and wants to take an in-service 401(k) loan before our vendor migration. Will a loan initiated now carry over, or should he wait until after the transfer? Any gotchas with repayment via payroll?

rick (Benefits): Good call to ask. Loans are plan-specific. If you start a loan with current vendor it generally transfers as a loan record, but some vendors require loan docs to be re-signed. Also repayments flow through payroll deduction codes — payroll needs consistent mapping during migration.

tina (Payroll): From payroll side: as long as the loan deduction code is present in the payroll file, deductions will continue. Migration risk: if deduction codes change or a participant ID remaps, deductions could stop. We recommend initiating the loan only after we confirm deduction code mapping in the cutover test.

theo (IC): Hmm. I need the cash now for a home repair. Is there a way to get a check from current vendor instead of payroll deduction?

rick (Benefits): Yes, vendors can often issue a distribution check for loans, but that triggers loan administration and possible withholding for taxable distributions if it's a taxable event. For a standard 401(k) loan, vendor sends check and you sign loan docs; repayment schedule is arranged. If you take it now, confirm with Payroll we'll map the deduction code in the migration.

emily (People Ops): Action items: 1) Rick to confirm whether the current vendor will transfer outstanding loans and whether re-signing is needed. 2) Tina to run a quick mapping check for loan deduction codes in PAY-2026-99 migration ticket. 3) Theo to confirm whether he wants vendor check vs payroll loan.

hr-bot: Ticket PAY-2026-99 created: "deduction code mapping + loan transfer check". ETA: 4 business days.

tina (Payroll): I've added loan deduction code to the test mapping. If Theo decides to proceed now and take a vendor check, payroll won't need to apply deductions immediately, but we'll need to re-enable payroll deductions once the loan is active and map the code on the new system.

theo (IC): I'll take the vendor check now. Please let me know if I need to re-sign anything after migration. Also what's the timeline for repayments showing on my paystub?

rick (Benefits): Repayments processed via payroll should appear the next payroll after vendor confirms the deduction code and participant ID. If we have to re-sign post-migration, there might be a 1-2 pay period gap. We'll flag this in the employee note.

emily (People Ops): Thanks. I'll log the decision and next steps in the migration tracker and notify Theo if any forms need re-signing. Quick handbook note: "If you take an in-service loan during vendor migration, expect possible short gaps in payroll repayment; coordinate with Benefits and Payroll to re-establish deductions after cutover."

hr-bot: PAY-2026-99 updated: loan deduction mapping verified for test; awaiting vendor loan transfer confirmation."
